newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open steady, eye on volatile baht.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open steady, eye on volatile baht.

text.p: Singapore shares opened steady on Wednesday recouping prior losses but sentiment was cautious in view of Thailand's decision to float the baht, dealers said.
"Investors are very cautious at this stage. They will be watching events out of Thailand on the baht," a dealer with a foreign brokerage said, noting a sharp drop in its value.
Thailand Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday the baht would be "managed floated", with its value determined by market forces, with immediate effect.
At 0225 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 1.69 points at 1,982.97.
Dealers said sentiment was also dampened by the absence of Hong Kong funds due to this week's long handover public holiday, and a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting.
Institutions were seen propping up some blue chips like the foreign tranche of UOB Bank, which rose to Singapore $15.10, up another 20 cents from the previous day.
Singapore Telecom dropped to S$2.69, down five cents on continuing liquidation, dealers said.
Meanwhile, the rights portion of Malaysia's Mulpha International saw high turnover, bid up to S$0.30. Dealers said they were not aware of any reasons for the uptick.
